Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

Introducing dark mode.

Enough of you asked. Starting today, every note screen in the app supports a dark theme: the editor, the sidebar, search, tags, everything. Open Settings > Appearance and pick Light, Dark, or System, and the app follows your OS setting automatically if you choose System.

We built this for two situations we heard about most: writing late at night without a bright screen in your face, and cutting battery drain on OLED phones, where a dark interface draws less power. Both were requests in our feedback inbox for months, and dark mode was consistently the top request in our roadmap poll.

A few details worth knowing. Syntax highlighting in code blocks now has its own dark palette, so contrast stays readable instead of just inverting colors. Exported PDFs still render on a white background regardless of your theme, since that's what most people expect when they share or print a note. And if you use custom note colors or highlights, we adjusted the palette so nothing washes out against the dark background.

The theme setting syncs across devices, so switching to Dark on your laptop switches your phone and tablet too, next time they connect.

This is the first version. We're watching for edge cases: third-party markdown themes, embedded images with white backgrounds, and PDF exports are the places most likely to need fixes, and we'll ship follow-ups as we hear from you.

Update to the latest version and switch it on in Settings. Tell us what still looks wrong.

The text above has these problems. Rewrite it so none remain.
Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.
